stories.title: Shooting at Oregon Elementary School Leaves Four Dead, Suspect Identified
stories.summary: A shooting at an elementary school in Bend, Oregon, resulted in the deaths of three children and one teacher. The shooter, identified as a former student, reportedly fired approximately 15 rounds, with additional ammunition found at the scene. A teacher and a community member intervened to stop the shooter, who was ultimately killed. A candlelight vigil was held to honor the victims.

stories.title: Katie Zacharia Leaves White House Press Secretary Role After Just Five Days
stories.summary: Katie Zacharia has exited her position as White House press secretary after only five days, stating it was an honor to serve. Reports indicate she was let go following public scrutiny and a series of blunders that distracted from President Trump's midterm campaigning efforts.

stories.title: Pope Leo XIV Discharged from Hospital After Lung Cancer Surgery
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV was discharged from Gemelli Hospital in Rome on Saturday after undergoing surgery to remove a cancerous tumor from his right lung. The 71-year-old pontiff had part of his lung removed and was deemed fit for discharge by his doctors, who confirmed his diagnosis of lung cancer earlier this week.

stories.title: Zelenskyy Calls for U.S. Sanctions on Russia After Trump Pauses Them
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy urged supporters to advocate for new U.S. sanctions against Russia, following President Donald Trump's decision to pause a package of sanctions aimed at the Russian economy. Trump's executive order, which he justified as being in the national interest, marks a significant shift in U.S. policy towards Russia amid deteriorating relations with Ukraine.

stories.title: Trump Suspends New Russia Sanctions Amid Tensions with Zelensky
stories.summary: The US president has temporarily waived several recently enacted sanctions against Russia, citing national interest. This decision has drawn criticism from Ukrainian President Zelenskyy, who expressed concern that it would embolden Russia's military actions. Trump did not provide further details on the rationale behind the suspension.

stories.title: Violence Erupts as Israeli Settlers Attack Palestinians During Olive Harvest in West Bank
stories.summary: Israeli settlers launched coordinated attacks on Palestinian villages in the West Bank during the annual olive harvest, resulting in injuries to several Palestinians and a Washington Post journalist. The settlers reportedly set fire to cars and olive trees, while also throwing rocks and using clubs against those attempting to harvest olives. The violence has been described as part of a pattern of yearly disruptions during the harvest season.

stories.title: Three Men Sentenced to 158 Years for Murdering Surfers in Mexico
stories.summary: A Mexican judge has sentenced three men to 158 years and nine months in prison each for the murders of Australian brothers Jake and Callum Robinson and their American friend Carter Rhoad. The trio was killed during a surfing trip in Baja California in 2024, reportedly during an attempted robbery.

Clashes have already occurred between police and protesters in major cities like Paris and Marseille. Tens of thousands are expected to participate in demonstrations across the country.

stories.title: Founder of India's 'Cockroach' Movement Released After Detention
stories.summary: Abhijeet Dipke, the founder of the Cockroach Janta Party, was released from detention a day after his arrest. His release followed an agreement to certain conditions, as confirmed by the party's head of legal affairs. Dipke gained attention earlier this year for leading a sit-in that contributed to the resignation of India's education minister.

stories.title: Children Bear Heavy Toll in DRC's Severe Ebola Outbreak
stories.summary: The Democratic Republic of Congo is experiencing its deadliest Ebola outbreak, with children particularly affected. Reports indicate that more than 1 in 4 of the deaths are among children, who face a staggering 60% fatality rate. This outbreak is caused by a rare strain of the virus for which there is currently no approved treatment.

stories.title: Iran Rejects Claims of Involvement in Houthi Attacks on Aden Airport
stories.summary: Iran has denied accusations of involvement in recent Houthi missile attacks on Saudi targets, including the international airport in Aden, Yemen. This denial follows Saudi Arabia's claims that Iran encouraged the Houthis' escalation against the kingdom. The Aden airport was struck by two missiles late on Friday, marking the second such incident in less than two weeks.

The announcement includes plans for elections in Tigray within six months. This move comes after the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF) lost control of the region.

stories.title: Zelensky Criticizes Trump's Sanction Waivers as Rewarding Putin
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has condemned US President Donald Trump's decision to waive sanctions on Russia, stating it only serves to reward Vladimir Putin. Zelensky expressed concern that Trump may continue to lift sanctions, particularly as tensions escalate in Ukraine. Meanwhile, Russia has celebrated the waiver as a 'historic' move, raising alarms in Ukraine about the implications for their ongoing conflict.
